title: ED Triage Crossroads
rulesTable: ESI 1: SBP<80 or SpO2<85 or GCS<9 or RR>35
ESI 2: stroke/STEMI alert, sepsis yes, SpO2<92, HR>130, chest pain age>=40, SI+, pregnant+abd pain, anticoag+head strike, immunosuppressed+fever, GCS<13 not explained by baseline AMS
ESI 3: chest pain/SOB/abd pain/fever/headache/neuro/psych default; fall age>=65; ESI 4: laceration, ankle, fall age<65; ESI 5: URI
72h bounceback: ESI one level more acute (min 2) for ESI 3-5
Sepsis yes: >=2 SIRS (T>=38.3 or <36, HR>90, RR>20) incl. temperature criterion with infection-type complaint; immunosuppressed + T>=38.0 -> yes
Stroke alert: neuro deficit with onset <=24 h; STEMI alert: chest pain + ECG STE
Isolation yes: MDRO history, or T>=38.0 with SOB/URI/fever
Area: ESI1 or stroke/STEMI -> resus; ESI2-3 -> main ED; ESI4 -> fast track (main ED if isolation); ESI5 -> waiting room (fast track if isolation)
Capacity: ESI2 with main ED full -> resus if a resus bay is free; ESI3 with main ED full -> waiting room; ESI4 with fast track full -> waiting room

glossary.ESI: Emergency Severity Index, 1 (resuscitation) to 5 (non-urgent). Sets placement tier and resource expectations.
glossary.confidence: The narrow agent's self-reported probability that its proposal is right. Low confidence raises queue priority.
glossary.trial category: A category a reviewer added with New…. It is logged and scored but never changes routing or fires alerts until promoted.
glossary.boarding: Admitted patients still occupying an ED room because no inpatient bed is free.
glossary.LWBS: Left without being seen: a waiting patient who leaves before evaluation.
glossary.door to room: Minutes from arrival to being placed in a treatment room.
glossary.census: Rooms occupied/total per area; (+n) = queued for that area; WR = waiting room.
glossary.priority: Queue order: uncertainty × error cost + wait time + domain urgency rules.
glossary.history conflicts: Agents are history-blind. A history rule (anticoag + head strike, immunosuppressed + fever, MDRO, 72h bounceback) gives a different answer than the proposal.
glossary.history relevant: A history flag bears on this decision, but the proposal is already consistent with it.
glossary.abnormal vitals: A vital sign is outside the safe triage range (SBP<90, SpO2<92, HR>120, RR>24, GCS<13).
glossary.capacity full: The proposed area has no free room. Accepting it queues the patient for that area.
glossary.high error cost: A wrong answer on this link is costly (missed alert, wrong page).
glossary.waiting: Domain minutes this decision has waited. Alert decisions waiting ≥10 min are high severity.
glossary.auto-pass: Confident, low-cost items without high-severity reasons are passed automatically; a sample goes to the spot-check queue.
glossary.spot-check: A random sample of auto-passed items for human review. Agree/disagree is logged as a quality signal.
glossary.what happens next: The downstream effect at the destination if you pass (or flip/change) this proposal.
glossary.PMH: Past medical history flags from the synthetic chart.
glossary.Prior ESI: Acuity assigned at the last visit.
glossary.Vitals trend: Triage vitals and repeats since arrival.
glossary.Capacity snapshot: Census at the moment this decision was emitted.
